newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 3.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a tax assessment that is likely to be defended in court, the Australian Tax Office has hit the debt-ridden holding companies of the former Adelaide Steamship empire with a record tax bill of A$876.9 million in relation to the A$1.05 billion profit made from the float of Woolworths by Industrial Equity Ltd in July 1994. Page 1.

Optus Communications new chief executive Peter Howell-Davies said yesterday pay-TV would be the company's main focus now that it had the backing of British giant Cable & Wireless. Howell-Davies said Optus was already in negotiations with other players on restructuring issues. Page 17.

Analysts believe shares in Mayne Nickless rose 33 cents yesterday on the back of news that Cable & Wireless plc had gained control of Optus Communications because Mayne's share effectively offered an option to buy shares in the upcoming Optus float. In adition, the market reacted well to promising news for Mayne. Page 17.

Following speculation software company Computershare Ltd may have cracked the United Kingdom market, shares in the company rose A$2.55 to A$12.00 yesterday. The rise comes as Computershare announced it had placed a 10 per cent equity stake with The Royal Bank of Scotland, and now sees it valued at A$269 million. Page 18.

In a further indication of the lack of faith in troubled gold producer Newcrest Mining, Mercury Asset Management Group has reduced its stake in Newcrest to less than 10 per cent. Despite acknowledgment of the efforts of Newcrest's new management, one fund manager said Newcrest's share price, which yesterday rose four cents to A$3.63, was "a hostage to the gold price". Page 19.

This week jewellery retailer Angus and Coote (Holdings) Ltd, Perth-based mining contractor Eltin Ltd, automotive parts supplier National Consolidated Ltd and Network Entertainment Ltd have all forecast flat or lower results. These announcements follow siilar predictions by RGC Ltd, Arthur Yates & Co Ltd and CarLovers Carwash Ltd last month. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a deal that will see it take over about A$33 million in debt, yet allows it to realise its dream of becoming a fully integrated force in the world cotton market, Queensland Cotton Holdings yesterday acquired private United States ginner Anderson Clayton for A$91.3 million. Page 23.

In his first public appearance after taking over at the helm of Optus Communications, Peter Howell-Davies indicated yesterday the main focus of the company following the effective takeover by Cable & Wireless would be the rationalisation of Australia's pa-TV industry rather than Optus' public sharemarket float. Page 23.

Adelaide Steamship Group subsidiary Industrial Equity Ltd was yesterday hit with a A$877 million Australian Tax Office bill. The bill could wipe out residual gains which may have been salvaged from the Adsteam collapse, and may force the group's bankers to suffer larger losses. Page 23.

The Uniting Church released a report of a fact-finding mission yesterday which recommends WMC rethinks its proposed development of the Tampakan copper project in Midanao because of ecological and human concerns, and called on the Federal Government to ensure the mistakes of Bougainville and Ok Tedi are not repeated in Mindanao. Page 23.

Westpac announced yesterday a A$695 million issue of mortgage-backed securities for the domestic market and a further offshore development in the eurobond market, moves that indicate the bank's confidence in continuing investor demand for that type of secrities, and will raise A$2.3 billion from securitisation. Page 23.

The Energy Users Group says the New South Wales Government's power levy introduced in the May Budget will cost the State's businesses' twice as much and will cost consumers A$275 million in 1999-2000. The group is concerned there is no clause in the legilation for a limit to be placed on the levy. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New Optus Communications chief executive Peter Howell-Davies says Optus is completely committed to restructuring the pay TV industry, an intention which may lead to a single programming company. Howell-Davies said Optus remained fully supportive of the Australian Rugby League. Page 33.

Communications Minister Richard Alston has announced that Primus Axicorp, AAPT, Optus Vision and Telstra Multimedia has been granted the first four carrier licences, after just a few days of deregulation. It is not yet understood why Telstra Multimedia an Optus Vision have sought the licences. Page 33.

The full Federal Court in Brisbane has upheld the decision that the Federal Police Commissioner has the right to search an accountants office for 'evidential material' in relation to the investigation of suspected tax schemes. Page 33.

Stronger than expected retail trade figures and a rise in building approvals has left the Reserve Bank questioning whether it should cut official interests rates. Market analysts believe yesterday's promising economic news will not lead to a cut in the rates. Page 33.

The Adsteam group has been hit by a A$877 million tax bill by the Australian Tax Office for back tax for the Adsteam-controlled Industrial Equity. The bill is due at the end of the month, with about A$400 million of the bill relating to additional tax, pealties and interest. Page 33.

The AMP Society, which intends to list on the Australian Stock exchange by the end of the year, has been criticised for not consulting its 2.2 million members about restricting ownership of the company by limiting shares to five per cent in the first 12 months of listing. Page 33.
THE AGE

In a further push for a restructuring of Australia's pay-TV industry, Optus Communications new chief executive Peter Howell-Davies says the industry is not providing consumers with what they wanted, and companies were not making acceptable returns. Howel-Davies said pay-TV was now a key management issue for Optus. Page B1.

Directors and senior executives of Melbourne stockbroker EL & C Baillieu have bought back the 40 per cent stake in the company owned by British investment bank NM Rothschild this week, giving them 100 per cent control of the company, and leaving Baillieu to seek a new partner. Page B1.

Queensland Cotton chief executive Richard Haire has announced that the company is world's largest non-government ginning company after it purchased the US-based Anderson Clayton for A$57 million. Page B3.

Advanta Corporation, which is being pursued for a takeover by the National Australia Bank, is being sued by shareholders for concealing information from investors after executives received A$51 million from selling the company's stock. Page B3.

The Japanese-owned multinational Toyota Australia, based in Melbourne, has announced that it will increase export sales to nearly A$500 million and raise export sales in 1997. Two hundred jobs have been created in recent months to cope with demand. Page 3.

Industrial Equity Ltd has been hit by an A$876.9 million bill by the Australian Taxation Department relating to back-taxes after four years of negotiations. The bill is due to be paid by the end of the month, but IEL have said they will lodge an objection Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
